_comment: #448 THE VETO BRANCH, END TO END. deep_descent already owns the ACCEPT branch (join Relc, boss dies, cleared_the_warren banks) and relc_descent_rewind owns the fork's snapshot geometry; neither carries the refusal to an OUTCOME, and until #448 the refusal had none worth carrying -- the veto fielded the JOIN pack with the ally slot empty and measured 0.04 competent-at-band, i.e. a refusal to win the act. The user ruling (CHOICE-LOG 2026-08-12) is that the veto is a hard-mode CHOICE, so the thing that needs proving in a canonical is that it is WINNABLE. Route: Continue into relc_veto_solo_start (already at the warren mouth, warrior L10 / Act III kit) -> interact the boss -> relc_descent -> [I go alone.] -> the confirm node, whose copy is pinned here because it is where the stakes are told -> [I'm sure. Hold the door. The rest is mine.] -> went_alone banks -> THE COMPOSITION PROOF: combat_started's exact initiative order is FOUR slots, no relc AND no raskghar_scout_2, so the fight is the entity's own `solo_enemies` and not the join pack minus an ally -> autoplay -> victory -> cleared_the_warren banks, the same key the join branch banks. Both branches therefore reach the same act gate, which is the whole point of the ruling: a different fight, not a different ending and not a wall.
seed_comment: Seed 3 nominal; the fixture's pinned rng_state (.seed=3-derived) governs the fight and OVERRIDES --seed. THE ODDS ARE NOT SLACK: this build reads floor-policy WIN 0.30 against the solo pack, so most states LOSE and this canonical needs the WIN. A re-derivation must run each candidate and confirm combat_finished victory:true; never hand-type a state (tests/_derive_rng_state.gd derives it from a seed).

steps._comment: Down 1 selects Continue, confirm loads the relc_veto_solo_start fixture.
The fixture stands the PC on (12,6) already facing DOWN onto the boss at (12,7), so no walk and no rng churn separates the load from the fight.
Down 1 = [I go alone.] (goto alone_confirm, no effects yet) -- the fork's gating is untouched by #448: same node, same option order, same effects.

THE STAKES PIN. The ruling asks the fork to telegraph what refusing costs, in voice and without meta numbers; this is that line, and pinning it means a silent rewrite reds a canonical instead of quietly un-telling the player.

payload_contains.speaker: Relc
payload_contains.text: Alone? Ha! You're either very brave or very— actually, no. Just the one thing. Fine. I'll cork the mouth so nothing gets in behind you, and that's every scrap of help you get. What's already in there stays in there with you, and it's bigger than both of us. People walk back out of that. Not many. Shout if you find teeth. Shout early.

steps._comment: Confirm on cursor 0 = [I'm sure. Hold the door. The rest is mine.] -> went_alone banks, ally_requires stays unmet, the solo fight starts.

steps._comment: THE #448 COMPOSITION PROOF, and the reason this is an order pin rather than a roster assert: assert_state cannot express key-ABSENCE, and both absences are the finding. FOUR slots (arrays compare element-wise) -- no `relc` (ally_requires unmet) and no `raskghar_scout_2` (the veto fields `solo_enemies`, a different pack). Contrast deep_descent's join fight, which carries six.
THE RULING, PROVEN: the refusal is winnable. This is the pinned-state WIN the fixture's own note warns is the minority outcome at this build.
Dismiss the victory banner (non-tutorial arena, confirm-then-hide).
steps.name: confirm

steps._comment: BOTH BRANCHES REACH THE SAME GATE. on_victory banks cleared_the_warren whichever way the fork went -- the veto is a different FIGHT, not a different ending and not a dead end.
And the ally never leaked in through the back: relc_joined_descent was never banked on this route.
